title: Correct reserved namespace prefix versus ordinary local name validation
api_or_output: Unchanged public API; ordinary element local xmlns and namespace-qualified attribute local xmlns are legal, while xmlns prefix/URI and plain declaration attribute remain reserved

acceptance.description: Clarify frozen tree wording and correct Tree/checked-builder/serializer validators per W3C Namespaces1.0: xmlns prefix and xmlns namespace URI are reserved, ordinary element local xmlns is legal, prefixed or namespaced ordinary attribute local xmlns is legal, unprefixed no-namespace attribute xmlns is a declaration and cannot be an ordinary attribute. Preserve namespace declaration representation and all xml binding rules, public shapes, validation precommit and error behavior. No new blanket DOM/syntax rejection.

Verify element/ordinary attribute/declaration distinctions with independently confirmed W3C/BCL cases, original forbidden prefix/URI/binding and atomic mutation checks, checked and trusted model replay paths, namespace Strict/Repair output and round trips using independent reference only (no unmerged DOM). Update only the two incorrect earlier negative expectations, replacing with stronger actual reserved-name regressions rather than weakening other tests.

Run focused and affected cumulative Tree/Serializer/builder/persistence/syntax checks, explicit approved actual public215/API models, independent source and fresh isolated local-package construction/serialization sample, relevant allocation checks and planning/committed diff/owned audit at known revision. No new scanning algorithm or workload change; reuse existing appropriate timing evidence unless genuine performance change requires exclusive measurements. Record exact corrected contract for DOM/corpus owners.

handoff.summary: Ordered conformance repair for verified Tree/serializer ordinary local xmlns rejection; standard reserves prefix/declaration shape, not arbitrary LocalPart. Required before trusted DOM/corpus integration.
